efet_body:
Chery recall expands to more than 27,000 cars in Australia, Indonesia and South Africa
Like in China and Malaysia, models are under scrutiny for manufacturing defects of the rear axle assembly

Share
Add to Preferred

Published

阅读简体中文版 (beta)
One of the affected models, the petrol-powered Omoda 5 SUV, is not sold in Singapore. PHOTO: OMODA
[SINGAPORE] China carmaker Chery’s recall of certain sport utility vehicle (SUV) models due to problems with the rear axle now includes more than 27,000 cars in Australia, Indonesia and South Africa.
This follows earlier
recalls for a similar issue
in China and Malaysia.
Based on an Australian government vehicle-recall notice published on Friday (Nov 13), a manufacturing defect on the rear axle assembly “may have been insufficiently welded and could crack”.
This could lead to a “loss of vehicle control, (and) will increase the risk of an accident which may cause injury or death to vehicle occupants and other road users”.
The recall notice affected 7,285 units of the 2023 Chery Omoda 5 SUV. Owners may check their vehicle identification numbers on the Australian government’s recall website.
A South Africa National Consumer Commission bulletin dated Nov 10 identified 17,508 Chery Tiggo 4 cars that were on sale from Oct 17, 2023, to Mar 27, 2024, as subject to recall, along with 2,685 Omoda C5 SUVs on sale from February 2023 to July 2026.

The bulletin stated that for both vehicle models, according to the supplier, the rear axle sleeve may have welding defects which could cause the rear axle to dislodge, resulting in rear suspension collapse.
Indonesia also recalled an unspecified number of Omoda 5 SUVs on Nov 10 for similar issues. A previous recall of 420 vehicles was carried out in May 2024.
In all cases, Chery agents in the respective countries will contact owners if action is required.

More
Follows China, Malaysia recalls
These moves follow earlier recalls in the Asia-Pacific region: China recalled around 54,000 Omoda and Tiggo vehicles (both brands made by Chery) on Nov 6, and
Malaysia recalled 9,500 Omoda
cars across two separate campaigns in May 2024 and October 2026.
The recalls were also related to issues with the rear axle.
The Business Times’
previous queries to Chery on those campaigns, including whether vehicles in the Apac markets were affected, were not answered.
The Omoda 5, a petrol-powered SUV, is not sold in Singapore. The Omoda E5 is a fully electric model from the same family, but has a different rear suspension assembly.
While vehicle recalls are common, they typically are minor in nature. Chinese brands have so far avoided any major, wide-ranging recalls, even as they focus on exports and enter right-hand-drive markets to
counter slowing domestic sales
.
China Passenger Car Association figures for the first 10 months of 2026 showed that domestic sales fell 22.3 per cent year on year to 15 million, while exports increased 74.6 per cent to 7.9 million.
However, Chery’s recall kicked off following major, widely reported incidents in Malaysia where the entire rear axle assembly – including the rear wheels – detached from vehicles.
The most recent incident occurred in Johor Bahru on Oct 10, resulting in Malaysia’s Road Transport Department suspending new registrations of the Omoda 5 the next day and announcing a technical investigation.

Honda, Toyota recall 1.6 million vehicles over Takata airbag rupture risk
There have been at least 28 deaths in the US stemming from defective Takata air bag inflators since 2009
Summarise
Share
Add to Preferred
Sources
Add to Preferred
Sources
Published
Sat, Nov 21, 2026 · 09:46 AM
— Updated Sat, Nov 21, 2026 · 10:12 AM
Honda and Toyota said there were no injuries or crashes tied to the vehicles being recalled, and there have been no airbag inflator ruptures. PHOTO: REUTERS
[WASHINGTON] Honda Honda and Toyota Motor said on Friday (Nov 20) they are recalling about 1.6 million cars, trucks and SUVs over a risk that Takata airbag inflators could rupture.
Honda and Toyota both said there were no injuries or crashes tied to the vehicles being recalled, and there have been no airbag inflator ruptures. The automakers will replace the airbag inflators in the recalled vehicles.
There have, however, been at least 28 deaths in the United States and more than 400 injuries stemming from defective Takata airbag inflators since 2009, an issue prompting the largest auto recall in US history.
All of those deaths involved airbag inflators without a drying agent. At least 20 of those deaths were in Honda vehicles.
The vehicles in the current recalls have airbag inflators that contain a moisture-absorbing material — unlike the millions of vehicles recalled previously.
The National Highway Traffic Safety Administration said analysis and inflator degradation simulation models conducted by independent testing groups allowed the automakers to act ahead of potential risks.

“Honda and Toyota saw early evidence of degradation risk in certain of their vehicles and are currently conducting proactive recalls of vehicles,” NHTSA said late Friday, adding that other automakers continue to conduct inflator analysis and testing.
The recall includes 810,592 older Honda cars and SUVs in the United States and 790,000 Toyota vehicles worldwide, including 314,000 in the United States.
The Toyota recall includes 2002-2010 Lexus SC430, 2011 IS250, 2017 GX460, 2003-2008 Toyota Corolla, 2005-2006 Tundra, 2005-2007 Sequoia and 2016-2017 4Runner. The Honda recall covers some 2013 Honda Accord, 2012-2013 Honda Civic, 2012-2013 Honda CR-V, 2013 Acura ILX and 2013 Acura RDX vehicles.

Subaru and Toyota picked the perfect time to roll out affordable EVs
The Honda recall covers vehicles originally sold or registered in 14 states or territories known for high temperature, humidity and large temperature fluctuations.
Over the past decade, two dozen major automakers have recalled more than 100 million vehicles fitted with Takata airbag inflators worldwide, including about 67 million vehicles in the United States.
Various automakers have also reported hundreds of injuries in vehicles since 2009 from Takata airbag inflators that can explode, unleashing metal shrapnel inside cars and trucks, killing or injuring drivers or other vehicle occupants.
Honda said long-term monitoring and analysis revealed potential propellant degradation in certain inflators within specific geographic regions.
Toyota warned that degraded propellant could cause the inflator to rupture if the airbag deploys and cause serious injuries.
The Honda recall applies to vehicles sold or registered in Alabama, California, Florida, Georgia, Hawaii, Louisiana, Mississippi, South Carolina, Texas, Puerto Rico, US Virgin Islands, Northern Mariana Islands (Saipan), Guam and American Samoa.
Toyota did not specify in which US states the recall applies but said it expects the replacement inflators will be ready by early 2027. REUTERS

efet_body:
Chery recalls about 54,000 vehicles in China after Malaysia axle-failure incidents
The carmaker has filed a recall for certain Omoda and Tiggo brand vehicles built between 2022 and end-2023
Summarise
Share
Add to Preferred
Sources
Add to Preferred
Sources
Derryn Wong
Published
Tue, Nov 10, 2026 · 06:09 PM
阅读简体中文版 (beta)
Chery will notify owners if any replacement of affected cars’ rear axle is needed, and will carry out the replacement at no charge. PHOTO: REUTERS
[SINGAPORE] China carmaker Chery Automobile has recalled around 54,000 vehicles of its Omoda and Tiggo brands over defective rear axles.
This follows previous recalls of Omoda cars in Malaysia, one of which followed a high-profile incident in Johor Bahru where the rear wheels of an Omoda 5 detached.
A notice published by China’s State Administration for Market Regulation on Friday (Nov 6) stated that the recall involves a total of 53,882 vehicles produced between Jun 6, 2022, and Dec 31, 2023.
This includes the Tiggo 5x sport utility vehicle and models from Omoda, although the notice does not specify which Omoda cars are involved.
It said that vehicles may have poor welds due to issues in the rear-axle manufacturing process. In extreme cases, the welds may fail and cause a loss of vehicle control.
The manufacturer will notify owners if replacement is needed and carry out the replacement at no charge.

has queried Chery on whether vehicles in Asia-Pacific markets, including Singapore, are affected.
Recall history
A photo from social media showing a Chery Omoda 5 with a detached rear axle in Johor Bahru, Malaysia, in October 2026.
PHOTO: PANGGIL AKU NAZ
The move follows two recalls for Omoda 5 vehicles in Malaysia, in 2024 and 2026, which cumulatively affected around 9,500 cars. Both recalls involved rear-axle defects, although Chery has not said whether all three recalls are related to the same issue.
The latest was in October this year, when Malaysia’s Road Transport Department, or Jabatan Pengangkutan Jalan,
suspended sales of the Omoda 5
and began a technical investigation. It is understood this involves Omodas assembled in Malaysia.

This followed a widely publicised incident in Johor Bahru on Oct 6, where an Omoda 5 around Aeon Mall Tebrau City lost its entire rear suspension, axle and wheels. Chery subsequently recalled 8,878 Omoda 5 cars in Malaysia.
As reported in BT, Singapore agent for Omoda, Vertex Automobile, said all cars sold here are made in China and not affected by the October recall.
The 2024 recall issue was traced to incomplete welds on the components arising from equipment miscalibration with components replaced in 60 cars.
Omoda entered the Malaysia market in July 2023 and the Singapore market in May 2024.
